paragraphs: Adversarial training strengthens a model by training it against deliberately perturbed examples. The quality of those perturbations matters: an attacker that exposes more weaknesses can provide a stronger training challenge. This paper focuses on how to generate such challenges efficiently while training is underway, complementing work on training losses and additional data.

The proposed method, A2, is a parameterized automated attacker. It searches a space of attackers for one suited to the current defense model and the examples being processed. This makes attack generation part of the ongoing training procedure. The central idea is to adapt the attacker to what it is trying to defeat, while keeping the additional computation low.

Across experiments on different datasets, A2 produces stronger perturbations with little extra cost and improves the robustness of several adversarial training methods against different attacks. These results support automated attacker selection as a useful way to strengthen existing training approaches. The reported benefit concerns both the effectiveness of the training perturbations and the robustness of the resulting models.
neurips-2022-a2-efficient-automated-atta.tldr: A2 adapts attack generation during adversarial training, producing stronger perturbations at low additional cost and improving robustness in experiments.

paragraphs: Human demonstrations contain multiple ways of behaving, and they usually lack reward labels. Learning from a large collection therefore requires representing several distinct behavior patterns without relying on rewards to identify desirable actions. Behavior Transformer, or BeT, addresses this problem by learning from demonstrations with multiple modes.

BeT adapts a standard transformer using action discretization and an action correction task. Discretization gives the model a way to represent distinct action alternatives, while correction supports predictions in a continuous action space. The correction mechanism draws inspiration from offset prediction in object detection. Together, these components let a transformer model varied behavior while still producing continuous actions.

The authors evaluate BeT on robotic manipulation and self-driving behavior datasets. It improves substantially over the prior methods considered at completing demonstrated tasks, while capturing the major behavior modes in the data. An ablation study examines the contribution of its key components. The findings indicate that task success and preservation of behavioral variety can be pursued together within this architecture.
neurips-2022-behavior-transformers-cloni.tldr: Behavior Transformer combines discrete action modeling with continuous corrections to learn multiple behavior patterns from demonstrations without reward labels.

paragraphs: Research on how the brain learns often studies biologically plausible approximations to gradient descent for recurrent neural networks. This paper asks whether those approximations affect generalization, beyond their ability to achieve task accuracy. Its focus is on the kinds of solutions different learning rules reach and how reliably those solutions perform beyond training.

The authors find that the biologically plausible rules studied generalize worse and less consistently than machine learning rules that follow the true gradient more closely. They connect this difference to the curvature of the loss landscape, which describes how sharply loss changes around a set of weights. Generalization is significantly correlated with curvature, and the biologically plausible rules tend toward regions of higher curvature.

Using dynamical systems tools, the paper develops theoretical arguments and a theorem explaining that tendency. The theory predicts the numerical findings and provides an explanation for the observed generalization gap. The authors also suggest possible remedies the brain could use. Those remedies are proposed possibilities, while the main contribution is an account of how approximate learning dynamics affect generalization.
neurips-2022-beyond-accuracy-generalizat.tldr: The paper links poorer generalization in biologically plausible recurrent-network learning rules to their tendency to reach high-curvature regions of the loss landscape.

paragraphs: Normalized advantage functions, or NAF, enable deep Q-learning with continuous actions by approximating the Q-function using functions that are quadratic in the action. This imposes a particular shape on how predicted value changes with the action. The paper asks when that restriction provides an acceptable approximation for the underlying decision problem.

The authors identify one suitable class: reinforcement learning problems produced by discretizing certain optimal control problems. Within this setting, they develop a new family of quadratic functions based on the NAF idea and prove approximation properties for it. The result gives a mathematical basis for using this type of action-value representation in the specified class of problems.

The paper then uses those approximation properties to propose several improvements to NAF. Experiments support the efficiency of the resulting changes. Its contribution connects the structure of an optimal control problem to the design of a learning algorithm: understanding where quadratic approximations are appropriate supplies both theoretical justification and practical directions for improving the method.
neurips-2022-continuous-deep-q-learning-.tldr: The paper proves useful quadratic approximation properties for a class of discretized optimal control problems and uses them to improve NAF.

paragraphs: Image-language pre-training commonly learns from paired images and text. Such pairs connect the two modalities, but the authors argue that existing approaches overlook semantic relationships among concepts. This paper investigates whether explicitly incorporating those relationships can improve the representations used for vision-language tasks and strengthen reasoning across modalities.

The proposed framework, Knowledge-CLIP, adds semantic information to CLIP through knowledge-based training objectives and several types of knowledge graphs. These graphs supply relationships that go beyond an individual image-text pairing. By including that information during pre-training, the method aims to align visual and linguistic representations more closely according to their meaning.

Experiments across a variety of downstream vision-language tasks demonstrate benefits over the original CLIP and competitive comparison methods. The paper reports improved semantic alignment and reasoning across scenarios and modalities. Its central contribution is a way to use structured conceptual knowledge within multimodal pre-training, with the experiments supporting the usefulness of that added information for subsequent tasks.
neurips-2022-contrastive-language-image-.tldr: Knowledge-CLIP incorporates knowledge graphs into CLIP pre-training to improve semantic alignment and performance on vision-language tasks.

paragraphs: Score-based generation relies on estimates of the score, the gradient of a distribution's log density, to guide sampling. This paper establishes polynomial convergence guarantees when the score estimate is accurate in the distribution-weighted squared-error sense. The guarantee applies to smooth distributions and depends polynomially on their log-Sobolev constant.

The analysis avoids the exponential growth of error over time and the curse of dimensionality present in earlier guarantees. It then studies the full generative procedure, which starts from white noise and uses score estimates at multiple noise levels to approach the learned data distribution. This connects a sampling guarantee to the mechanism used in score-based modeling.

Annealing plays an essential role in the proof: progressing through noise levels supplies a suitable starting distribution for each next step. This gives theoretical support to the practical importance of that gradual procedure, without establishing that every possible method must use it. The authors also show that combining predictor and corrector steps yields better convergence than either component alone.
neurips-2022-convergence-for-score-based.tldr: The paper proves polynomial sampling guarantees from accurate score estimates and explains the benefits of annealing and predictor-corrector sampling.

paragraphs: Neural networks often increase and decrease feature resolution to process images at multiple scales. Common spatial up-sampling operators depend heavily on local pixel information. This paper develops an alternative in the Fourier domain, where the representation supports global modeling, so increasing resolution can draw on relationships beyond nearby pixels.

The difficulty is that Fourier features do not follow the same local similarity property that makes spatial interpolation straightforward. The authors study how representations at different resolutions relate across the spatial and Fourier domains. From these relationships, they derive transformation rules that support their proposed operator, FourierUp.

FourierUp combines a two-dimensional discrete Fourier transform, rules for increasing the Fourier dimensions, and an inverse transform. It can be integrated directly into existing networks. Experiments report consistent improvements across object detection, segmentation, image de-raining, dehazing, and guided super-resolution. These results support frequency-domain up-sampling as a broadly useful network component, with the theoretical analysis supplying the rationale for how its resolution change is performed.
neurips-2022-deep-fourier-up-sampling-83.tldr: FourierUp increases feature resolution through Fourier-domain transformations and improves performance across several vision tasks.

paragraphs: Graph anomaly detection seeks unusual entities within a network of relationships. Because anomalous examples are rare and applications differ, the available datasets strongly shape what researchers can investigate. This paper introduces DGraph, a real-world financial graph that includes changing relationships over time, expanding the data available for studying this problem.

DGraph contains roughly three million nodes, four million dynamic edges, and one million nodes with ground-truth information. The authors examine how anomalous and normal nodes differ in their surrounding structure, distributions of neighbors, and temporal behavior. Their observations indicate that these groups generally have different patterns across all three aspects.

The analysis also suggests that the two million background nodes are essential for identifying fraudsters. This highlights the importance of the wider graph context alongside the nodes with ground-truth information. Extensive experiments accompany the dataset analysis. Together, they position DGraph as a resource for exploring how financial anomalies relate to both network structure and changes over time.
neurips-2022-dgraph-a-large-scale-financ.tldr: DGraph provides a large dynamic financial graph whose analysis highlights structural, temporal, and background-node information for anomaly detection.

paragraphs: Learning relationships across distant parts of a sequence is an important challenge in sequence modeling. Structured State Space models, known as S4, had delivered strong results on long-range tasks using a particular structure for their state matrices. This paper investigates how much of that structure is needed to retain the observed performance.

S4 represents a state matrix with a diagonal component and a low-rank correction, supporting efficient computation. The authors remove the correction and use diagonal state matrices alone. Their resulting Diagonal State Space model, or DSS, is conceptually simpler and straightforward to implement. The change isolates whether the extra matrix structure is essential on the evaluated tasks.

DSS matches S4 on Long Range Arena tasks and speech classification using the Speech Commands dataset. These findings show that a simpler state-space parameterization can preserve performance in these settings. The contribution is an empirical simplification of a successful architecture, narrowing the gap between the complexity of its matrix construction and the components needed for the reported results.
neurips-2022-diagonal-state-spaces-are-a.tldr: DSS uses diagonal state matrices alone and matches S4 on the evaluated long-range and speech-classification tasks.

paragraphs: Class imbalance means some categories have much less training data than others. Common responses change how heavily examples count in the loss or adjust classification margins. This paper examines what happens to optimization under those methods by studying each class's loss landscape, giving particular attention to minority classes.

The authors analyze the spectrum of the Hessian, which describes curvature around the network's weights. They observe that training reaches saddle points in the minority-class loss landscapes. This suggests that minority-class performance can suffer from the geometry of the reached solution. They then investigate optimization methods designed to escape such points.

The paper provides theoretical and empirical support for using Sharpness-Aware Minimization, or SAM, to escape minority-class saddle points. Although SAM encourages flatter minima, it also helps address the saddle behavior identified here. The authors report a 6.2% increase in minority-class accuracy over Vector Scaling Loss and an overall average increase of 4% across imbalanced datasets. The findings connect improved generalization to the optimization landscape of underrepresented classes.
neurips-2022-escaping-saddle-points-for-.tldr: The paper identifies minority-class saddle points during imbalanced learning and shows that SAM can escape them and improve generalization.

paragraphs: Time-series forecasting can be difficult when observations cover only a short period and contain substantial noise. The paper addresses this mismatch between limited data and deep models through generative modeling. Its method, D3VAE, combines a bidirectional variational autoencoder with diffusion, denoising, and disentanglement.

A coupled diffusion model augments the time-series data without increasing aleatoric uncertainty, the uncertainty associated with randomness in the observations. It also makes inference with the autoencoder more tractable. The authors incorporate multiscale denoising score matching into the diffusion process to guide generated series toward the true prediction target.

D3VAE additionally treats its latent representation as multivariate and reduces total correlation to disentangle its components. This part of the design aims to improve prediction stability and interpretability by reducing dependence among latent variables. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data report substantial gains over competitive algorithms. The approach brings together data augmentation, guidance of generated outputs, and organization of the latent representation to address forecasting from limited, noisy observations.
neurips-2022-generative-time-series-fore.tldr: D3VAE combines diffusion, denoising, and disentangled latent variables to improve forecasting from limited and noisy time-series data.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to predict the outputs of a linear dynamical system when observations are noisy and incomplete. A dynamic filter maintains an internal state to make those predictions. Directly optimizing such a filter is difficult because its internal-state representation can introduce degeneracies that obstruct convergence guarantees.

The authors address this issue through informativity. Intuitively, every component of the filter's internal state should represent something about the true state of the underlying system. They show that this property overcomes the degeneracy and introduce a regularizer that explicitly enforces it. The regularizer changes the optimization problem so that useful internal representations are maintained.

The proposed algorithm combines gradient descent on the regularized objective with a reconditioning step. For this output-estimation problem, the authors prove convergence to the globally optimal cost at a rate proportional to one over the number of iterations. The result supplies a global guarantee for direct policy search in this partially observed linear setting and identifies internal-state informativity as the mechanism that makes the guarantee possible.
neurips-2022-globally-convergent-policy-.tldr: An informativity regularizer and reconditioning step give direct policy search a global convergence guarantee for filtering partially observed linear systems.

paragraphs: Hierarchical agglomerative clustering builds a hierarchy through successive merges, making it appear inherently sequential. This is a major obstacle when clustering very large graphs. The paper introduces ParHAC, a parallel approximation algorithm for average-linkage clustering, and analyzes both its computational requirements and its practical performance.

For a graph with m edges, ParHAC provides a (1 + epsilon) approximation using nearly linear total work and polylogarithmic parallel depth. Work measures overall computation, while depth captures the length of dependent computation that parallelism cannot remove. The authors also show that comparable bounds for exact average-linkage clustering are impossible under standard complexity assumptions, giving a theoretical reason to allow approximation.

On large real-world datasets, ParHAC achieves an average 50.1-fold speedup over the best sequential baseline considered, with quality similar to exact clustering. It also clusters a graph containing 124 billion edges in a little over three hours on a commodity multicore machine. These results connect the parallel complexity guarantees to substantial practical scalability.
neurips-2022-hierarchical-agglomerative-.tldr: ParHAC makes approximate average-linkage graph clustering highly parallel, combining nearly linear work with strong practical speedups.

paragraphs: An unsuccessful adversarial attack does not by itself establish that a model is robust. The attack's optimization procedure may have failed to find a weakness that exists. This paper addresses that evaluation problem by developing automatic diagnostics for gradient-based attacks, making robustness checks easier to debug systematically.

The authors categorize attack failures according to their effects on optimization. Their analysis identifies two previously unreported failures affecting popular implementations and earlier evaluations. They then propose six indicators that automatically detect signs of these problems during attack optimization, together with a protocol for applying the corresponding fixes.

Experiments involving more than fifteen models across three application domains show that these indicators can improve existing robustness evaluations. Their value is to reveal when an attack result may reflect a faulty search process and to help repair that process. The paper presents this as an initial concrete step toward automated, systematic evaluation, with evidence that diagnostic tools can make attack-based assessments more dependable.
neurips-2022-indicators-of-attack-failur.tldr: Six automatic indicators and a repair protocol help detect attack optimization failures that can make models appear falsely robust.

paragraphs: Structured kernel interpolation accelerates Gaussian process inference by approximating a covariance function using inducing points arranged on a grid. A dense grid supports efficient matrix operations, but its size grows exponentially with input dimension. This paper tackles that growth by replacing the dense grid with a sparse one.

Sparse grids retain accurate interpolation while requiring a number of points that grows more slowly with dimension. Using fewer points is only part of the challenge, because the resulting kernel matrix must still support fast computation. The authors therefore develop a nearly linear-time algorithm for multiplying that matrix by a vector.

The paper also combines sparse grids with an efficient interpolation scheme based on simplicial complexes. Together, these changes adapt both the grid representation and the operations needed to use it. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that structured kernel interpolation can reach higher dimensions while maintaining accuracy. The contribution is a coordinated approach to reducing grid growth without giving up the computational advantages that motivate the framework.
neurips-2022-kernel-interpolation-with-s.tldr: Sparse grids and fast matrix operations extend structured kernel interpolation to higher-dimensional Gaussian process problems while maintaining accuracy.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning a pretrained model on a device lets it adapt to locally collected sensor data without sending that data to the cloud. Tiny devices, however, often lack the memory for conventional training. This paper combines algorithm and system changes to make visual recognition transfer learning practical with only 256KB of memory.

Two methods address different obstacles. Quantization-Aware Scaling calibrates gradient scales to stabilize training with 8-bit values. Sparse Update avoids computing gradients for less important layers and parts of tensors, reducing the resources needed for backpropagation. Together, they address both the difficulty of optimizing low-precision networks and the cost of updating them.

The Tiny Training Engine implements these methods by pruning backward computation and moving automatic differentiation work from runtime to compilation. The framework matches the reported accuracy of PyTorch and TensorFlow while using less than one-thousandth of their memory. The result demonstrates on-device adaptation on tiny microcontrollers and provides a practical basis for devices to keep learning from new data after deployment.
neurips-2022-on-device-training-under-25.tldr: Gradient scaling, selective updates, and a specialized training engine enable visual transfer learning on devices with only 256KB of memory.

paragraphs: When distributions are represented by samples, optimal transport methods try to estimate an unknown transport map. Choosing parameters or selecting among candidate maps is difficult because the true map is unavailable. This paper proposes a quantitative selection criterion based on the Brenier formulation of optimal transport.

The theoretical guarantee relates the selected map's quadratic error to the best candidate's error, with a distortion factor depending on smoothness and strong convexity and an additional statistical deviation term. The criterion is estimated through convex optimization. It supports comparisons among entropically regularized transport, input convex neural networks, and smooth, strongly convex nearest-Brenier models.

The authors also examine what this selection criterion means for domain adaptation. In a standard experiment, it identifies the potential closest to the true transport map between source and target distributions. Yet that potential is far from the best for downstream transfer classification. This finding separates accuracy at estimating the transport map from success on the subsequent task, showing that the two objectives need not select the same solution.
neurips-2022-parameter-tuning-and-model-.tldr: A Brenier-based criterion selects accurate transport maps, while an experiment shows that transport accuracy need not yield the best transfer classifier.

paragraphs: Observational data may support a range of possible treatment effects rather than a single identifiable value. Partial identification seeks bounds on that range. This paper develops a method for bounding average treatment effects in general causal graphs using implicit generative models that can contain both continuous and discrete variables.

Continuous treatments introduce a difficulty because their average treatment effects are generally non-regular. The authors address this by defining a regular approximation from partial derivatives of response functions. They call this quantity the uniform average treatment derivative, or UATD. It provides an alternative target for optimization while retaining a connection to the treatment-effect question.

For linear structural causal models, the authors prove that their algorithm converges to tight bounds on average treatment effects. For nonlinear models, the evidence is empirical: optimizing with UATD produces tighter and more stable bounds than directly optimizing the average treatment effect. The paper thus combines a guarantee for the linear setting with an experimentally supported strategy for handling the more difficult nonlinear case.
neurips-2022-partial-identification-of-t.tldr: Implicit generative models and a derivative-based treatment-effect approximation enable tight linear-case bounds and more stable nonlinear-case estimates.

paragraphs: Performative power measures how much a firm operating an algorithmic system can causally change the behavior of a participating population. The paper proposes this concept as a way to study competition in digital markets, where traditional analysis can struggle to define the relevant market. Its identification requires little knowledge of market internals.

The theory links this power to a firm's incentives. With low performative power, optimizing its objective on current data is the best it can do. High power creates opportunities to benefit by steering behavior. In a simple theoretical model, monopolies maximize this power, personalization increases it, and competition and outside options reduce it.

The authors propose an observational causal design based on discontinuities in how platforms display content. This lets causal effects from existing platform studies serve as lower bounds on performative power. The paper thereby connects a theoretical measure to observable behavior. Its discussion of competition policy and antitrust remains speculative, proposing a possible role for the concept rather than establishing a policy prescription.
neurips-2022-performative-power-e633e530.tldr: Performative power measures a platform's causal influence on participants and connects that influence to competition, personalization, and possible policy analysis.

paragraphs: A Gaussian mixture represents a distribution using several Gaussian components, but the appropriate number of components may be unknown. This paper studies efficient model selection for one-dimensional mixtures. It also allows the observed distribution to differ slightly from a mixture, so the guarantee accommodates approximation error in the modeling assumption.

Given a distribution within epsilon in total variation distance of a k-component mixture, the algorithm uses polynomially many samples and polynomial running time in k divided by epsilon. It returns a Gaussian mixture whose component count is close to k and whose error is close to epsilon, up to logarithmic factors. This approximately identifies the smallest useful model size.

The result improves the tradeoff described for earlier algorithms, which either produced substantially more components or required time exponential in k. Its significance is that computational efficiency and a compact mixture representation can be obtained together under the stated proximity condition. The authors also adapt their techniques to obtain similar reconstruction results for Fourier-sparse signals.
neurips-2022-robust-model-selection-and-.tldr: The paper efficiently learns compact univariate Gaussian mixtures from approximately mixture-distributed data, with guarantees up to logarithmic factors.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a scene from multiple images involves separating geometry, materials, and illumination, all of which influence appearance. The paper shows that a more realistic shading model using ray tracing and Monte Carlo integration substantially improves this decomposition. The challenge is making that model usable inside gradient-based reconstruction.

Monte Carlo integration produces noisy estimates, even with many samples, and this noise makes optimization difficult. The authors incorporate multiple importance sampling and denoising into an inverse rendering pipeline. These additions improve convergence and allow optimization with low sample counts, addressing the computational and numerical difficulty introduced by the more realistic renderer.

The resulting method jointly reconstructs explicit triangle-mesh geometry, materials, and lighting. It substantially improves separation of material properties from illumination compared with previous work. This matters because a reconstructed scene should account for which aspects of appearance come from the surface and which come from the light. The results support the authors' argument that denoising can be a useful integral component of high-quality inverse rendering.
neurips-2022-shape-light-and-material-de.tldr: Combining realistic Monte Carlo rendering with sampling and denoising improves joint reconstruction of scene geometry, materials, and lighting.

paragraphs: Compressive sensing seeks to recover a signal from relatively few linear measurements. A generative network can constrain recovery by restricting the signal to its output range. Earlier theoretical guarantees for Gaussian-weight networks required layers to expand. This paper asks whether recovery remains possible when some layers become narrower.

The authors prove recovery for signals in the range of a Gaussian generative network when layer widths are proportional to the input-layer size, up to logarithmic factors. Because the requirement compares widths with the input size, it permits a layer to contract relative to the preceding layer. This relaxes a structural restriction that differs from the architecture of many practical generators.

The proof introduces a weaker matrix concentration condition called the Range Restricted Weight Distribution Condition. Gaussian matrices satisfy this condition, allowing the authors to replace the stronger condition used in earlier analyses. They also discuss how this substitution extends existing results for phase retrieval, denoising, and spiked matrix recovery to non-expansive generative priors under the relevant assumptions.
neurips-2022-signal-recovery-with-non-ex.tldr: A weaker matrix condition extends generative-prior signal recovery guarantees to Gaussian networks that can include contractive layers.

paragraphs: Models can fail outside their training distribution when they rely on correlations that change across environments. Invariant Risk Minimization aims to avoid this by keeping the expected label, conditioned on learned features, consistent across environments. This paper identifies a fundamental flaw in that formulation that explains failures of its practical version, IRM-v1.

The authors propose a complementary invariance principle called MRI. It reverses the conditioning: the expected features, given a label, should remain consistent across environments. They show that this formulation avoids the identified flaw and introduce MRI-v1 as a simplified practical implementation. The change alters what relationship the method requires to stay stable.

For general linear problems, the paper proves that MRI-v1 yields invariant predictors when sufficiently many environments are available. In nonlinear image-based experiments, MRI-v1 strongly outperforms IRM-v1 and consistently approaches optimal out-of-distribution generalization. The theoretical guarantee depends on the linear setting and environment condition, while the nonlinear findings provide empirical evidence for the value of the complementary principle.
neurips-2022-the-missing-invariance-prin.tldr: MRI reverses IRM's conditioning to enforce a complementary invariance, with conditional linear guarantees and strong nonlinear experimental results.

paragraphs: A mixture-of-experts layer uses a router to activate selected expert networks for an input. This paper investigates why that architecture can improve learning and why its experts need not collapse into one effective model. Empirical observations point to two important ingredients: clusters in the underlying problem and nonlinear expert networks.

Motivated by those observations, the authors construct a challenging classification problem with intrinsic cluster structure. They prove that a single expert, such as a two-layer convolutional network, has difficulty solving it. A mixture whose experts are themselves two-layer convolutional networks can solve the problem successfully.

The analysis explains how this advantage arises: the router can learn features representing cluster centers and use them to divide the overall problem into simpler classification subproblems. Individual experts can then handle those subproblems. This provides a theoretical mechanism for useful specialization in the studied setting. The result helps explain how routing and expert nonlinearity can cooperate, with the formal claim tied to the structured classification problem analyzed.
neurips-2022-towards-understanding-the-m.tldr: For a structured classification problem, the paper proves that learned routing lets multiple nonlinear experts solve tasks that challenge a single expert.

paragraphs: Video instance segmentation requires understanding individual objects across a sequence. VITA approaches this by asking whether condensed, object-specific information can provide the context needed for offline video analysis. It builds on an existing transformer-based image instance segmentation model, using its detector to produce object tokens for each frame.

VITA associates those frame-level tokens to build relationships across the video. Its video-level processing does not use spatio-temporal backbone features. This separates sequence understanding from the detailed features produced by the image backbone and concentrates it on the object information distilled by the detector.

With a ResNet-50 backbone, VITA reports state-of-the-art results of 49.8 AP on YouTube-VIS 2019, 45.7 AP on YouTube-VIS 2021, and 19.6 AP on OVIS. The token-based design also supports long, high-resolution videos on a common GPU and allows the frame-level detector trained on images to remain frozen. These findings support object-token association as both an effective representation for video understanding and a useful architectural separation for practical processing.
neurips-2022-vita-video-instance-segment.tldr: VITA links object tokens across frames to achieve strong video instance segmentation results while supporting long, high-resolution videos.
